title: Aubergine Lasagne
subtitle: Roasted aubergine and tomato lasagne with béchamel
excerpt: Aubergine lasagne layers roasted sliced aubergine with a rich tomato sauce and creamy béchamel. The aubergine, when properly roasted until golden and collapsed, has a silky, meaty texture that makes this one of the most satisfying vegetarian pasta bakes. Related to parmigiana, it adds pasta sheets to that classic format.
sourceNotes: Aubergine lasagne is a southern Italian-influenced dish that draws on the traditions of both pasta al forno and parmigiana di melanzane. Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, documents aubergine preparations from southern Italian cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen covered at 180°C for 50 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate unbaked.

content.text: Aubergine lasagne uses thickly sliced, roasted aubergine as the main filling, layered with tomato sauce and béchamel between pasta sheets. The key is roasting the aubergine properly: it needs to be golden and fully collapsed before it goes into the dish, not half-raw and spongy. Under-roasted aubergine releases water as it bakes and produces a wet, bitter result. Roasted properly, it is silky and rich.

Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C / gas mark 7). Arrange the {{aubergine}} slices in a single layer on two roasting tins. Brush generously with 4 tablespoons of olive oil and season with salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and fully collapsed. Set aside.
Make the tomato sauce and béchamel

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a saucepan. Cook {{onion}} of onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{salt-table}} of salt. Simmer for 15 minutes. Tear in {{basil}} of basil leaves and stir through.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter, add {{plain-flour}} of flour, stir for 2 minutes. Whisk in {{whole-milk}} of warm milk gradually and stir over medium heat until thick, about 5 minutes. Season with {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg and a pinch of salt.

Reduce oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the base of a large baking tin. Add a layer of {{lasagne-sheets}} sheets. Spread half the tomato sauce, then half the roasted aubergine, then a layer of béchamel and some {{parmesan}} of Parmesan. Repeat: pasta, remaining tomato sauce, remaining aubergine, béchamel, Parmesan. Finish with pasta, remaining béchamel, and Parmesan on top.
Cover with foil. Bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake for a further 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The lasagne is wet and the filling is bitter
items.cause: The aubergine was undercooked before layering and released water during baking.
items.fix: Roast the aubergine until it is completely golden and collapsed, not just softened. It should look slightly deflated and caramelised at the edges. The bitterness comes from uncooked aubergine.

items.cause: The sauce was not reduced enough before assembling.
items.fix: Simmer the tomato sauce until it has thickened noticeably, about 15 to 20 minutes. A thin sauce combined with moisture from the aubergine makes the finished dish watery.

content.text: Aubergine lasagne sits between classic northern Italian lasagne and southern Italian parmigiana di melanzane, which layers fried aubergine with tomato and mozzarella without pasta. The lasagne version adds pasta sheets and béchamel to the southern combination. It is a good summer dish when aubergines are at their best and cheapest. Mozzarella can replace some of the Parmesan for a stretchier, milder result.
